correctedCritiques.con-reason-incarnation-access-gap: Strongest feature: The hypothetical separates conclusions available through abstract natural reasoning from contingent historical and biological information indispensable to identifying Jesus as divine and human, testing the affirmative’s accessibility claim. Principal limitation: It cannot exclude a generic divine particularity or embodiment concept, so the scenario must distinguish conceptual inferability from the inability to name Christianity’s earthly person and history. Live burden: The side must establish that metaphysical structure alone cannot yield Christianity’s identifying incarnational content, while conceding whatever abstract conclusions unaided reason legitimately supports. Locked score: The very strong band reflects precise relevance, restrained questioning, representational charity, and decisive exposure of the epistemic access gap, tempered because absent historical information does not disprove every incarnational metaphysics.
correctedCritiques.pro-infer-divine-self-knowledge: Strongest feature: The reply separates exhaustive comprehension from limited rational inference, preventing human cognitive limitations from foreclosing every justified conclusion concerning how a perfect mind possesses self-knowledge. Principal limitation: That valid distinction does not authorize the falsification-driven process attributed to God and leaves divine self-knowledge, falsifiable self-relation, and their connection underspecified. Live burden: The affirmative must derive this process from acknowledged divine attributes, differentiate inference from speculative projection, and explain why perfect self-knowledge requires more than immediate knowledge of perfection. Locked score: The mixed band recognizes epistemological clarification, complete contact with both objections, and comparatively strong relevance, while retaining concerns about underdetermination, unstable process terminology, limited evidential warrant, and failure to establish the positive divine attribution.
